# Fomoraij · Book II, pp. 136–143
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	136
P	The <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210) damned themselves. Oh, they'll tell you they had no other choice. That their treacherous servants drove them to it. That they knew not the cost. That they were lied to by the <b>Things</b> <b>Below</b> (page 412). But, no, they knew what they were doing. They just didn't care.
P	And why would they have cared? Had they not lost everything? Had they not been driven from their homes and hunted like beasts, by the very servants they had created? By those who owed them <i>everything</i>?
P	So, yes damn you, the Green Lords made their deals. They called up the darkness and the poison. Let it flow through their minds. Their flesh. Their lands.
P	And when not even that was enough to turn the tides, when they were betrayed again—this time by their fellow <b>Makers</b> (page 264)—and they were corralled into one last trap… well, what did they care?
P	What could they care? Let the traitors have the surface. For now.
P	And so, twisted and mad with hatred, they went below. Into the bosom of their masters. There, they wait. They spawn new horrors. They hate.
P	And one day, perhaps, they will return.
H2	Names
HR
P	Slavic-sounding, but with more vowels and softer consonants: Aawnaswasiya, Blaagu, Doogromil, Eleema, Loobimoor, Miwooslawa, Oolliyanaw, Rabomoor, Weelimir, Yoanaw
H2	Hooks
HR
B	<b>Infected servants</b> (page 140) are watching villagers near the <b>Stream</b> (page 396)
B	An earthquake opens a crack in a cave bear's den, exposing them to a Fomoraij's lair and influence
B	Hunters/trappers go missing, then turn up weeks later horribly mutated
B	A Fomoraij's minions steal children from their beds and drag them to their master
B	<b>Forest Folk</b> (page 150) glyphs show people filing into a cave, laden with gifts (for the Fomoraij that secretly entranced them)
PAGE	137
H2	Dwellers beneath
HR
P	The Fomoraij have dwelt beneath the Great Wood for centuries. Their influence can be felt, certainly, and they sometimes send forth minions, but they have not seen the surface since the fall of <b>Vor Svetelik</b> (page 468).
P	To create a Fomoraij, start with 2 themes from the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412).
P	Combine with a constraint that keeps it from emerging, the nature of its lair, and 2-3 forms. Give it a name and perhaps an ominous title. Write it up as a threat (a <i>villain</i>, a <i>beast</i>, or a <i>magical entity</i>). If the PCs are likely to fight it, also write it up as a monster (see example on page 142).
P	1d12 constraint
HR
P	1-2 Confinement: by accident, by artifice, by its own size or nature (<b>Instinct</b> to capture others, to escape)
P	3-4 Disdain: of the world above, of the world that betrayed them (<b>Instinct</b> to punish anything that reminds it of its past)
P	5-6 Decay: of its mind, its power, its sense of self (<b>Instinct</b> to lash out)
P	7-8 Fear: of the Fae, of the Makers, of the much-hated light (<b>Instinct</b> to see threats everywhere)
P	9-10 Obsession: with hoarding, experimenting, digging, etc., to the exclusion of all else (<b>Instinct</b> to pursue its obsession)
P	11-12 Patience: it waits, it gathers power, it makes preparations (<b>Instinct</b> to further its plans)
P	<b>1d12</b> lair
HR
P	1 A yawning cavern, flooded; dotted with islands and unlikely structures
P	2 Endless rough-hewn tunnels, like an ant hive
P	3 An inverted forest of roots, tubers, fungus hanging from the ceiling
P	4 A series of underground streams, rivers, lakes, all teeming with horrors
P	5 A deep, vertical shaft ending at a vault of white stone
P	6 Tunnels and chambers, every inch lined with bones
P	7 The petrified belly of a gargantuan, primordial <b>titan</b> (page 303)
P	8 Vaulted tunnels lined with roots of iron-infused wood, rusted and bleeding
P	9 Limestone caverns, the walls pulsing with <b>red crystal</b> (page 424)
P	10 Limestone caves and columns, wet and dripping, festooned with slimy life
P	11 Strangely smooth tunnels coated in warm, pulsing organic material
P	12 A vast chamber of white stone, a mighty dead tree growing down from the ceiling Fomoraij lairs are always found underground and beneath the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200), accessed via caves and <b>Green Lord</b> <b>ruins</b> (page 214). The sites above are often corrupted by the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412).

P	10 Slimy/oozing/mucous

P	<i>The PCs have encountered some horrors</i> <i>in the Great Wood—some crinwin</i> <i>oozing silver slime and wasps with</i> <i>hallucinatory venom. I already decided</i> <i>that these things were corrupted by the</i> <i>Things Below, based on the themes of</i> <i>"insanity/chaos/ruin/quicksilver" and</i> <i>"corruption/disease/poison/vermin."</i>
P	<i>Now I'm thinking that a Fomoraij is</i> <i>behind them. I keep the two themes, and</i> <i>roll a</i> constraint <i>of "confinement." For</i> <i>its</i> lair<i>, I roll "a series of underground</i> <i>streams, rivers, lakes, all teeming with</i> <i>horrors." For its</i> form<i>, I get "too many</i> <i>limbs/eyes/mouths," and "a swarm of</i> <i>smaller things" and "slimy/oozing/mucous." I ponder, and come up with:</i> <i>Yaarowslow the Many is trapped away</i> <i>on an island in an underground lake,</i> <i>fed by tiny rivulets of groundwater. It</i> <i>has transformed its flesh into an oozing,</i> <i>silvery nest, host to an endless swarm</i> <i>of skittering and buzzing horrors that</i> <i>serve as its eyes and hands and mouths.</i> <i>For centuries, the vermin have burrowed through stone to reach the surface.</i> <i>It has recently succeeded, and its silvery</i> <i>spawn now taint a spring deep in the</i> <i>Great Wood.</i>

B	A polished slice of agate the size of a dinner table, bringing nightmares and dark thoughts to those who linger in its presence (<i>immobile</i>, Value 2)
B	A pair of what seem to be rubies (Value 3) set as the eyes of a horrible statue; they're actually <b>red crystals</b> (page 424) and impart a cruel bloodlust on whoever holds them.

ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	Bloodshot amber
P	◇ each, <i>magical</i>
P	1d4 fist-sized gems, riddled with red-black intrusions.
P	When you <b><i>drip blood onto an amber</i></b>, name a manifest spirit in your presence and roll
P	+CHA. If the spirit has an intact <b>tether</b> (page 358), roll with disadvantage. <b>On a</b> <b>10+</b>, the spirit is imprisoned in the amber;
P	<b>on a 7-9</b>, the amber starts to suck the spirit in, but it may yet fight back; <b>on a 6-</b>, the spirit wrests free and the amber shatters.
P	When you <b><i>imprison a spirit in a bloodshot</i></b> <b><i>amber</i></b>, it is wracked with pain and cannot manifest. Only one spirit can be imprisoned at a time. When you <b><i>touch the amber with</i></b> <b><i>bare skin</i></b>, you can communicate with the spirit within and release it if you want (even if you weren't the one who imprisoned it).
P	When a bloodshot amber is found, it likely contains a spirit that has been trapped in agony for centuries.
HR
ICON	icons/site.svg
H3	Dream-lily pool
P	A raised pool of clear water. A strange lily grows within, its tendrils pouring over the lip and coating the floor, hiding bleached bones. The tendrils rustle when living things approach, and a gentle wind promises prophecy and wisdom.
P	When you <b><i>let a lily-tendril slither under</i></b> <b><i>your skin</i></b>, take 1d4 damage (ignores armor) and fall deeply asleep. Roll +WIS: <b>on a</b> <b>10+</b>, you dream of wisdom—ask the GM any question and get a helpful, honest answer, though one cloaked in symbolism; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you dream of wisdom (as on a 10+) but also of hunger, desperation, and want—mark a debility when you wake; <b>on a 6-</b>, you are trapped in endless nightmare—mark two debilities and you shall not wake unless you find an exit or someone rescues you from without.
P	Regardless, your dreams are clearly visible in the waters of the pool. You get the sense that something else may be watching, too.

H3	Infected servant
P	Fomoraij sometimes ensnare beings of the world above, capturing them, luring them in with promises of power, or compelling the weak-willed to attend them.
P	They then infect the victim, turning them into extensions of their will.
P	Start with a base creature, and then pick or roll for the nature of the infection, the means of control, and up to 3 gifts. Interpret them based on what you know about its master. Update the base creature's tags, stats, qualities, instinct, and moves accordingly.
P	1d12 infection
P	1-2 A bug/worm/vine, burrowed into their brain/spine
P	3-4 A foul substance, injected/inhaled/ imbibed
P	5-6 A fungus/plant, growing under their skin
P	7-8 A spirit possessing their body, bound by intricate scars/tattoos
P	9-10 A mass of vermin/a single horror, eating them from the inside out
P	11-12 One or more shards of <b>red crystal</b> (page 424) embedded in their skull
P	1d12 means of control
HR
P	1-2 By crushing their will
P	3-4 By eating away at what they once were
P	5-6 By filling them with euphoria/ pleasure
P	7-8 By promising them power/immortality/revenge/a cure/etc.
P	9-10 By wracking them with pain
P	11-12 Roll 1d10 twice, or make up something new
P	If you like, roll 1d6 for the extent of control.

P	<b>1d12</b> gift
HR
P	1 A <i>reach</i>, <i>near</i>, or <i>far</i> attack (tentacles, spitting globs, flung spines, etc.)
P	2 A terrifying presence; an ability to spread panic/fear/horror
P	3 An area attack (cloud of poison, blast of nettles, psychic scream, etc.)
P	4 An amorphous/malleable/ shapechanging form
P	5 An ongoing link to its master, an ability to share senses/thoughts/ words/power
P	6 A way to spread its infection and/ or its master's influence (intentionally, incidentally, or both)
P	7 Camouflage/stealth/ability to avoid notice
P	8 Exceptional strength/speed/ferocity/deadliness
P	9 Influence/control over the minds of others
P	10 Minions/servants/ability to send out extensions of itself
P	11 Mobility (jumping, flying, climbing, burrowing, squeezing, etc.)
P	12 Unnatural resilience/vigor/durability
P	Should a PC or an important NPC become infected by a Fomoraij (or one of their servants), write it up as a threat (an <i>affliction</i>). If a PC willingly becomes an infected servant, consider creating a playbook insert, using the <b>Thrall</b> for inspiration (see
P	<i>Book I</i>, page 152).

P	<i>I want a big scary servant of</i> <b><i>Yaarowslow the Many</i></b> <i>(page 142), a</i> <b><i>hagr</i></b> <i>(page 208) that stumbled on the tainted</i> <i>spring. I roll "a foul substance, injected/</i> <i>inhaled/imbibed" and think of Yaarowslow's silvery slime. I get "by eating</i> <i>away at what they once were" as a means</i> <i>of control, and imagine the silver slime</i> <i>corrupting it from the inside, replacing its</i> <i>blood and organs and overwhelming its</i> <i>mind with voices and delusions. For gifts,</i> <i>I pick "unnatural resilience/vigor/durability" and "a way to spread its infection</i> <i>and/or its master's influence." I then roll</i> <i>for a third gift and get "an area attack."</i>
P	<i>I update the hagr's stat block to reflect</i> <i>these changes, and end up with this:</i>
P	INFECTED HAGR
P	Solitary, large, terrifying, hardy,
P	magical
P	HP 20; ARMOR 4 (resilience), 1 vs.
P	bronze (blubbery hide)
P	DAMAGE meaty hands d10+3 (hand, close, grabby, forceful) or tree trunk d10+5 (reach, area, crude, forceful) or hurled heavy thing d10+3 (thrown, forceful)
P	SPECIAL QUALITIES infectious blood; suffers from delusions, behaves erratically INSTINCT to spread its master's influence
P	> Fix someone with its evil eye, inflicting overwhelming delusions
P	> Pluck things from the ground as if weightless
P	> Obsessively carve its master's sigils into things
P	> Fly into a senseless rage

H3	"Typical" Fomoraij
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>cunning</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 26; <b>Armor</b> 4 (resilience), 0 vs. bronze <b>Damage</b> mighty blows d12+3 (<i>hand</i>,
P	<i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> can sense anything that happens in its lair (but might not think to)
P	<b>Instinct</b> [Use constraint as a guide]
P	• Overawe anyone in its presence
P	• Twist, mutate, or transform living things with a gesture
P	• Wield nearby plants and beasts as extensions of itself
P	• Regenerate wounds from anything but <b>orichalcum</b> (page 162)
P	No Fomoraij is truly typical; use the stats above as a starting point. A Fomoraij's constraint (page 137) dictates its instinct. Add or change its tags, stats, special qualities, and moves based on the themes (page 416), constraint, lair, and forms (page 137) that you've identified.
P	<b><i>Yaarowslow the Many</i></b> <i>is a mass of flesh</i> <i>that oozes infectious silvery slime, and the</i> <i>host of skittering, slithering, and buzzing</i> <i>horrors that serve as an extension of its will.</i>
P	YAAROWSLOW, THE MANY
P	Solitary, large, magical, terrifying, amorphous
P	HP 24; Armor 5 (resilience, lacks organs),
P	2 vs. bronze (thick hide)
P	DAMAGE spurts of corrosive slime d10+1 (hand, close, area, messy, 1 piercing)
P	SPECIAL QUALITIES largely immobile, hive-mind connection with its vermin swarms; half damage from stabbing or smashing
P	INSTINCT to escape
P	> Overwhelm foes with horror and thousands of squealing voices
P	> Infect minds and bodies with silvery slime
P	> Wield its swarms and its silvery slime as an extension of itself
P	> Regenerate wounds from anything but orichalcum

P	SWARM OF SILVERY VERMIN
P	Horde, terrifying, amorphous, fearless
P	HP 6; ARMOR 5 (resilience, lacks organs),
P	1 vs. bronze DAMAGE bites and stings d6 (hand,
P	1 piercing)
P	SPECIAL QUALITIES hive-mind connection with Yaarowslow; can fly/crawl/burrow/swim; unharmed by piercing/cutting weapons; takes half damage from smashing weapons; vulnerable to area affects (like naphtha fire).
P	INSTINCT to do Yaarowslow's will
P	> Engulf a victim
P	> Inject infectious silvery slime
P	> Scatter and reform elsewhere
